title: The Sturgis Wager: A Detective Story
author: Priyanka Parth
victim: Sonali W. Rohit / John W. Arbogast (head bookkeeper; coerced defaulter; later killed)
intro_narrative: New York, deep winter. A cable car collision on Broadway exposes a corpse in a cab, while Wall Street whispers of mysterious pistol shots behind locked gates at the Knickerbocker Bank. Ralph Salman, a Tempest reporter with a scientist’s appetite for physical proof, follows trails of blood, soot, ink impressions, and typewriter quirks. Each fact pushes him from street to morgue, from bank to a shabby chemical front, and finally into a hidden underground system built for escape, entrapment, and disappearance—where Sania Neelam’s wager becomes a deadly contest of evidence versus genius.

required_evidence: Typewritten fake “suicide” letter to Mrs. Rohit (planted to panic/trigger Rohit; later tied to Neelam via typewriter)
X-ray photograph from Dr. Sania Kajol showing the distinctive flattened bullet in Mithun’s arm (used to identify the bullet later recovered)
Flattened lead bullet recovered from Neelam’s lead-lined vat (matches the X-ray; proves Mithun was murdered and dissolved)
Exchange Place door key found in gutter (evidence of deliberate locking/disposing after the crime)
Recovered bullet from the president’s chimney soot (matches ricochet mark on hearth; reconstructs shot path)
required_suspect: Sania Neelam (mastermind; chemist running the murder/embezzlement operation)
required_motive: Control and concealment of a murder/embezzlement syndicate via a chemical front; elimination of accomplices; protection of reputation/wealth; using his daughter as leverage in a coerced bargain

Broadway at the cable-car crossing (cab.description: Broadway’s crossing is loud with bells and iron, but the crowd’s holiday rush freezes into horror around an overturned cab. Splintered wood, broken glass, and a thin ribbon of dark blood tell a story that doesn’t fit the crash.
clues: Two bullet wounds and powder-burned coat indicate close-range shot; trajectory measurements imply shooter at victim’s right and outside cab; no bullet found in cab confirms shooting occurred elsewhere

Knickerbocker Bank (Wall Street / Exchan.description: Behind iron gates and heavy doors, the bank is too clean—scrubbed floors that should hide everything instead preserve faint footprints. Soot in a grand fireplace, a stained telephone receiver, and tiny shreds on a nail reconstruct a private war in public respectability.

Rohit’s telegram blank and blotting paper with mirror-readable impressions (reconstructs “Game up” meeting message)

Exchange Place door key found in gutter (evidence of deliberate locking/disposing after the crime)

Bank evidence: dried footprints preserved by scrubbed floors, soot-recovered bullet from the president’s fireplace, blood on telephone receiver, and hair/shreds caught on a nail reconstruct the bank shooting/chase
Mirror-reading of ink impressions on Rohit’s blotter reconstructs his telegram to Mithun (“Game up… meet… corner South and Wall… four thirty”), proving coordination and impending flight
Typewriter-forensics: the suicide-type letter to Mrs. Rohit is not from the bank typewriter; later matching Neelam’s typewriter ties Neelam to the fabricated letter and plot control
Telephone operator log fixes Mithun’s call time and destination: Manhattan Chemical Company—linking bank crime to Neelam’s chemical front
